resources.string: Requests Android’s sustained performance mode while Minecraft is active. On supported devices this lowers short peak clocks to reduce thermal throttling and improve frame-time consistency during longer sessions.
Sustained performance mode is not supported by this device.
Lower values improve performance; higher values improve image quality. Changes apply the next time Minecraft starts.
Enter a value from %1$d%% to %2$d%%. 100%% uses the normal screen size.
When enabled, Minecraft uses immersive fullscreen and hides the Android system bars. Display-notch behavior is controlled separately by Ignore display notch.
Allows the gameview to ignore rounded corners of your device by adding a small inset.
Controls Minecraft’s framebuffer size and aspect ratio. The Resolution Scale percentage above is applied to this base resolution, except MCSX which stays fixed at 1280 × 960.
Experimental — use at your own risk. Unsupported resolutions can cause stretched UI, black screens, renderer crashes, or poor performance. Restart Minecraft after changing this option.
Choose the base framebuffer and aspect ratio Minecraft will use. 1920 × 1080 automatically rotates to 1080 × 1920 when the game is portrait. MCSX uses its recommended fixed 1280 × 960 framebuffer.
This changes Minecraft’s framebuffer and visible aspect ratio. Some renderers, mods, or devices may not support it correctly. Use this option at your own risk.
Enter the exact base framebuffer width and height. Values from %1$d to %2$d pixels are allowed. The existing Resolution Scale is applied afterwards.
Enter width and height values from %1$d to %2$d.

Keeps Minecraft chat/text fields visible by moving the game view above the Android keyboard. Enabled by default. Turn this off when using a floating keyboard or when you do not want the game view to move.
